title: Taking Care of My Body
intro: My body is my very own. When I wash it, brush it, and keep it clean, I feel fresh, happy, and ready to play!

items.say: Your private parts are the parts that go under your underwear. They get dirty just like the rest of you, so they get a bath wash too.
steps: Use warm water.
Use a little bit of gentle soap.
Wash softly. No hard scrubbing.
Rinse until all the soap is gone.
Remember: these parts are private. Only you wash them, or a safe helper who is teaching you.

items.say: Ears get dusty on the outside, just like a table does.
steps: Get a warm, wet washcloth.
Put the cloth over your finger.
Wipe around the outside of your ear, nice and gentle.
Never push anything inside your ear hole.

items.say: Your belly button is a tiny dent. Dirt likes to hide in there!
steps: Do this at bath time.
Put a little soap on your finger.
Gently wipe inside your belly button.
Rinse it clean.

items.say: Your toes have little hiding spots between them. Dirt and wetness like to sit there.
steps: Put your feet in soapy water.
Wiggle your toes like little worms.
Dry between every toe with a towel.

items.say: Deodorant is a helper that keeps your armpits from getting stinky.
steps: Put your clothes on first.
Swipe up and down under one arm 2 or 3 times.
Swipe up and down under your other arm 2 or 3 times.
Count it out loud: 1, 2, 3!

items.t: Taking care of cuts and scrapes
items.say: A cut or a scrape is a boo-boo on your skin. Boo-boos need care so they can get better.
steps: Rinse the boo-boo under cool water.
Pat it dry.
Cover it with a cute bandage.
Tell a helper you got a boo-boo.
items.o: Taking care of cuts and scrapes

items.t: Knowing when I need to pee or poop
items.say: Your tummy and bottom send you a message when it is time to go. It feels like a pushy, full feeling.
steps: Notice the full, pushy feeling.
Stop playing right away.
Walk to the bathroom.
Do not wait. Waiting can make an accident.
items.o: Knowing when I have to pee or poop

items.t: Wiping after I use the bathroom
items.say: Wiping gets your bottom clean after you go.
steps: Take your time.
Wipe with toilet paper. Use a moist wipe if you need it.
Look at the paper.
Keep wiping until the paper is clean.
Moist wipes go in the trash can, not the toilet.

items.say: Brushing washes away sugar bugs that can hurt your teeth.
steps: Brush in tiny circles.
Keep going for 2 whole minutes.
Brush the top, the bottom, the front, and the back!

items.say: Floss gets food out from the tight spots where your brush can't reach.
steps: Pick a colorful floss pick.
Slide it gently between two teeth.
Do this one time every day.

items.say: Your tongue gets yucky too, so it gets brushed.
steps: Stick your tongue out.
Sweep it softly from the back to the front.
Do it 3 times.

items.say: Skin folds are the squishy creases, like in your elbows and tummy and legs. Wetness hides in them.
steps: Wash gently with soap.
Pat the folds all the way dry with a soft towel.

items.say: Your neck and chin get sweaty and drooly, so they need washing.
steps: Tilt your chin up.
Wipe in gentle circles with a warm, soapy cloth.

items.say: Fingernails grow and grow, and dirt hides under them. A helper clips them.
steps: Ask a helper after bath time.
Wait for your nails to get soft in the water.
Hold still while your helper clips.

items.say: Toenails need trimming too, so they don't poke you.
steps: Cut straight across.
Make sure the corners do not poke your skin.

items.say: Shampoo makes your hair clean and soft.
steps: Close your eyes tight.
Rub the shampoo in like you are making bubbles.
Rinse it out really well.

items.say: Conditioner makes hair smooth so brushing doesn't hurt.
steps: Put a drop the size of a penny on the ends of your hair.
Count to 10.
Rinse it out with water.

items.say: Brushing helps get the tangles out.
steps: Start at the bottom ends of your hair.
Then brush a little higher.
Then work up to the top.

items.t: Washing my hands after the bathroom
items.say: Germs are teeny tiny and you can't see them. Soap and water wash them away.
steps: Wet your hands and put on soap.
Scrub while you sing Happy Birthday two times.
Rinse and dry.

items.t: Washing my hands before I eat
items.say: Clean hands keep germs out of your tummy.
steps: Scrub your palms.
Scrub the backs of your hands.
Scrub your fingers.
Then sit down and eat.

items.t: Blowing my nose into a tissue
items.say: A tissue catches the yucky stuff when your nose is runny.
steps: Press one side of your nose shut.
Blow out softly.
Throw the tissue away.
Wash your hands.
items.o: Blowing my nose into a tissue

items.t: Pulling my pants up and down
items.say: Pants need to be in the right place for the potty.
steps: Pull them all the way down to your knees before you sit.
When you are done, pull them up to your waist.

items.say: Flushing sends the pee and poop away.
steps: Push the handle down.
Hold it until the water swirls.
Close the toilet lid.

items.say: Soap that stays on can make your skin itchy.
steps: Rinse your body with water.
Rinse until your skin feels clean and smooth.
No slippery soap should be left.

items.say: Your face gets a wash every day.
steps: Splash cool water on your face.
Wipe gently with a soft washcloth.
Pat it dry.

items.say: Toothpaste foam is for spitting, not swallowing.
steps: Lean over the sink.
Spit out the foam.
Take a tiny sip of water and rinse your mouth.

title: My Clothes and My Space
intro: Picking cozy clothes and keeping my room neat helps me feel comfy and organized.

items.say: Different weather needs different clothes.
steps: Look outside, or check the weather.
Cold day? Wear a sweater.
Sunny day? Wear shorts!

items.say: Matching means clothes that look nice together.
steps: Pick your favorite colors that go together.
Or ask a helper to help you pick an outfit.

items.say: Each shoe has its own foot. A left shoe goes on the left foot. A right shoe goes on the right foot.
steps: Put the two shoes side by side.
Look at the inside curves.
When they look like they are hugging, they are the right way!

items.say: Clean clothes smell nice. Dirty clothes need to be washed.
steps: Has food on it? It is dirty.
Smells funny? It is dirty.
Wore it all day? It is dirty.
Toss dirty clothes in the hamper.

items.say: Folding keeps clothes neat so they fit in the drawer.
steps: Lay the shirt flat.
Fold the sleeves in.
Fold it in half.
Put it neatly in the drawer.

items.say: A routine is the same steps in the same order, every day. It helps you know what comes next.
steps: Look at the picture chart.
Do the first step.
Check what step comes next.
Do the same for morning and for bedtime.

items.t: Putting on clean underwear every day
items.say: Clean underwear keeps your private parts fresh and comfy.
steps: Wash up in the morning.
Put on clean underwear right after washing or getting dressed.
Dirty underwear goes in the hamper.

items.say: Tied laces keep your shoes on your feet.
steps: Make bunny ears with the laces.
Cross them over each other.
Pull one loop through.
Pull it snug!

items.say: Buttons and zippers close up your clothes.
steps: For buttons: push the button halfway through the hole.
Then pull it the rest of the way from the other side.
For zippers: hold the bottom still and pull the zipper up.

items.say: When you finish playing, your things go back home.
steps: Pick up 5 things at a time.
Put each one in its home spot.
Pick up 5 more until it is done.

items.say: A clean table is ready for the next meal.
steps: Wipe from the back of the table to the front.
Wipe the crumbs into your hand or a napkin.
Throw the crumbs away.

items.say: A made bed looks cozy and neat.
steps: Pull the pillow up to the head of the bed.
Pull the blanket all the way up to the pillow.

items.t: Checking the doors are locked at night
items.say: Locked doors help keep your home safe while you sleep.
steps: Walk to the front door with a helper.
Walk to the back door with a helper.
Check that both locks are turned.

title: Food, Water, and Kitchen Safety
intro: My tummy tells me when I am hungry and when I am full. Water and healthy food give me energy to play and grow. The kitchen has hot and sharp things, so I stay safe there.

items.say: Your body is thirsty all day long. Water helps you feel good.
steps: Keep a water bottle near you.
Take 3 big gulps every hour.

items.t: Knowing if I am hungry or full
items.say: Your tummy talks to you. It can say, "I am hungry!" or "I am full!"
steps: Ask your tummy before you eat.
Ask your tummy while you eat.
Ask your tummy after you eat.
items.o: Knowing when I am hungry or full

items.say: A butter knife is for spreading and cutting soft food. Be careful with it.
steps: Keep your fingers away from the blade.
Press down gently on soft food.

items.say: Stoves, ovens, and hot pans can burn you very badly.
steps: Stay 3 big steps back from the stove.
Stay 3 big steps back from the oven.
Stay 3 big steps back from hot pans.

items.say: You can make an easy snack all by yourself.
steps: Pick an easy snack, like an apple, a banana, or a cheese stick.
Get it from the fridge.
Put it on a plate and enjoy!

items.say: You can make toast or a sandwich with a helper.
steps: Spread butter softly across the bread.
Ask an adult to help push down the toaster.

items.t: Putting food back in the fridge
items.say: Cold food stays yummy in the fridge. Out on the counter, it goes bad.
steps: When you are done pouring, put the milk back.
Put the yogurt back right away too.

items.t: Knowing what is safe to eat
items.say: Only real food is for eating.
steps: Only put real food from the kitchen or your plate in your mouth.
If you are not sure, ask a helper first.
items.o: Knowing what is safe to eat

items.say: Closed lips keep food in your mouth and are nice for people near you.
steps: Take a small bite.
Close your lips together.
Chew 10 times before you swallow.

items.say: Slow and steady keeps the drink in the cup.
steps: Hold the cup with both hands.
Tilt it slowly.
Swallow before you take another sip.

items.say: Food can go bad. Bad food can make your tummy sick.
steps: Does it smell sour?
Does it look funny or have spots?
Show a grown-up first. Do not eat it!
items.o: Knowing if food smells bad or spoiled

items.say: Forks and spoons help you scoop up your food.
steps: Hold the handle like a pencil.
Scoop up a bite.
Bring it to your mouth.

items.t: Wiping my mouth after I eat
items.say: Food can stick on your face and fingers.
steps: Use a napkin.
Wipe the corners of your mouth.
Wipe your fingers clean.

title: Staying Safe and Being Kind
intro: My body belongs to me. I know about privacy, safe touches, and staying away from danger. I am gentle with other people and with animals.

items.say: Your private parts are the ones under your underwear. They are yours, and they stay covered and private.
steps: Keep them covered with clothes.
Keep the bathroom door closed.

items.t: Safe touch and my body boundaries
items.say: Your body belongs to you. You get to say what feels okay and what does not.
steps: If a touch feels wrong, say loudly, "Stop, I don't like that!"
Go tell a safe helper right away.
You are never in trouble for telling.

items.say: Personal space is the invisible bubble around you.
steps: Keep one arm length between you and other people.
Let other people have their bubble too.

items.t: Who to call in an emergency
items.say: An emergency is when someone is hurt or in danger and you need help fast.
steps: Learn how to dial 911.
Know your safe helper's phone number too.
items.o: Knowing who to call in emergency

items.say: Cars are big and fast. They cannot stop quickly.
steps: Hold a grown-up's hand.
Stop at the curb.
Look left. Look right. Look left again.

items.say: A scab is a little cover your body makes so a cut can heal.
steps: If your scab itches, put a band-aid over it.
Or pat it gently.
Do not scratch or pick it.

items.t: Taking medicine only with a grown-up
items.say: Medicine can help you, but it can hurt you if you take the wrong kind or too much.
steps: Never touch medicine bottles or pills.
Only take medicine that a safe helper gives you.
items.o: Taking medicine only with adult help

items.say: Helpers can only help if they know where it hurts.
steps: Point to the spot that hurts.
Say, "My [head / tummy / arm] hurts right here."

items.t: Telling when I feel sick or dizzy
items.say: Dizzy means the room feels like it is spinning. Sick means your tummy or body feels yucky.
steps: Sit down on the floor right away.
Call out to a helper.
Say, "I feel sick!" or "I feel dizzy!"
items.o: Telling when I feel sick or dizzy

items.t: Never opening the door to strangers
items.say: A stranger is someone you do not know. Never open the door for a stranger.
steps: When someone knocks, freeze!
Go get a grown-up.
Let the grown-up open the door.

items.say: The bathroom is a private place.
steps: Close the door all the way.
Then take off your clothes or sit on the potty.

items.say: Cleaning liquids can hurt your body if they get in your mouth, eyes, or skin.
steps: Leave spray bottles alone.
Leave soap pods alone.
Leave all cleaning liquids alone.

items.t: No hitting or biting when I am mad
items.say: Mad feelings are okay. Hitting and biting hurt people.
steps: Squeeze a pillow.
Stomp your feet two times.
Or hug yourself tight instead.
items.o: Not hitting or biting when mad

items.t: Being gentle with pets and animals
items.say: Animals have feelings too. They like gentle touches.
steps: Use a soft, flat hand.
Pet from head to back, slow and gentle.
items.o: Being gentle with pets and animals

items.t: Hurting people or pets is not okay
items.say: Hurting someone or an animal is wrong. It makes them feel scared and sore.
steps: Keep your hands gentle.
Use your words when you feel mad.
Do not use your hands or feet to hurt.
items.o: Hurting people or pets is wrong

items.say: You already know this one! Great job!
steps: Ask clearly, "May I play with this, please?"
Ask before you touch someone else's things.

title: Big Feelings and Feeling Safe
intro: Sometimes my heart and mind have big feelings. I might feel scared, worried, sad, or heavy. I have skills that help my body feel calm and safe again.

items.say: Feelings have names, like mad, sad, and scared. When you say the name, the feeling gets smaller.
steps: Look at the feelings cards.
Or say out loud, "I feel [mad / sad / scared] right now."

items.say: Slow breathing tells your body, "You are okay."
steps: Smell the flower: breathe in through your nose.
Blow out the candle: breathe out through your mouth.
Do it a few times.

items.say: A break helps your mind rest when things feel like too much.
steps: Say, "I need a 5 minute quiet break, please."
Walk into a calm room.
Rest until you feel better.

items.say: Your safe helpers love you. They want to help you fix problems.
steps: Think of your safe helpers.
Remember they love you.
Tell them when something is wrong.

items.say: Everybody makes mistakes. Mistakes help your brain learn.
steps: Say, "Mistakes help me learn."
Say, "I can fix it, or try again next time."

items.t: Knowing when my body is tired
items.say: Your body needs rest, just like a phone needs charging.
steps: Notice your heavy eyes or a big yawn.
Put screens away.
Lie down and rest.
items.o: Knowing when my body is tired

items.say: Sometimes worry thoughts buzz around in your head like bees. They are loud, but you can calm them down.
steps: Name 3 blue things you can see in the room.
Take 3 slow belly breaths.
Or squeeze a fidget toy.

items.say: Sometimes your body shakes or feels scared, even when you are okay. You can help it settle.
steps: Put one hand on your heart and one on your tummy.
Do blow-out-the-candle breaths.
Or wrap up in a weighted blanket.

items.say: Sometimes you feel sad for a long time, like you are wearing a heavy backpack. It is okay, and you do not have to carry it alone.
steps: Wrap up in a warm blanket.
Hug a stuffed animal.
Tell a helper, "I feel heavy today."

items.t: Getting stuck in bed or in a chair (Depression)
items.say: Sometimes your body feels too heavy to move. You can start with a tiny step.
steps: Wiggle your toes.
Then sit up.
Then take 1 sip of water.
items.o: Getting stuck in bed or chair (Depression)

items.say: Sometimes something you see, hear, or smell brings back an old scary feeling. You are safe now.
steps: Say to yourself, "I am safe right now in this room."
Touch 3 solid things around you.

items.say: A flashback is when your mind feels like the scary thing is happening again. It is a memory. It is not happening now.
steps: Look at your feet on the floor.
Rub your sensory cube.
Say out loud, "Today is ____ (say the day). I am safe."

items.t: Feeling jumpy or watching for danger (PTSD)
items.say: Sometimes your body keeps watching for danger, even when it is safe. It is trying to protect you.
steps: Sit with your back against a sturdy wall.
Hold a pillow tight.
Take deep breaths.
items.o: Feeling jumpy or watching for danger (PTSD)

items.say: Sometimes you don't feel safe in your own body. These steps help you feel your body again.
steps: Press your feet hard into the floor.
Squeeze your hands into fists, then let go.
Sip some cold water.

items.t: Monsters and scary movie things are pretend
items.say: Monsters on a screen are made up by people.
steps: Remind yourself, "That is a costume, makeup, or a cartoon drawing."
items.o: Monsters and scary movie things are pretend

items.t: Shadows and night noises cannot hurt me
items.say: At night, shadows and creaky sounds can seem spooky. They are just shadows and house sounds.
steps: Turn on your nightlight.
Look at the shadow's shape.
Remember, houses creak when they settle.
items.o: Shadows and night noises cannot hurt me

items.say: People on TV are actors. They are playing pretend, just like when you play with toys.
steps: Remember: actors are pretending.
Cartoons are drawings that move.

items.t: Bad dreams are just thoughts in my head
items.say: A bad dream is a story your brain makes while you sleep. It is not real.
steps: Wake up and look around your bedroom.
Hug your blanket.
Say, "The dream is gone. I am safe."
items.o: Bad dreams are just thoughts in my head

items.say: True words tell what really happened. Pretend words are for fun games.
steps: Tell what really happened first.
Then, if you want to play pretend, say, "Let's make up a fun game!"

items.t: Saying sorry when I make a mistake
items.say: Sorry shows you care about someone's feelings.
steps: Look at the person.
Say softly, "I am sorry I bumped you. Are you okay?"
items.o: Saying 'sorry' when I make a mistake

title: Talking, Listening, and Pausing
intro: I talk with other people in kind ways. I take turns, use a gentle voice, and can pause a habit when it is time to do something else.

items.say: Everybody needs help sometimes. Asking is brave and smart.
steps: Take a deep breath.
Ask, "Can you help me with this, please?"

items.say: Talking is like a ball. You throw it, then the other person throws it back.
steps: Say your thought.
Pause.
Ask, "What do you think?"

items.say: People have a bubble. Sometimes they want it to be bigger.
steps: If someone looks away or steps back, give them space.
Take two big steps back.

items.say: Inside voices are quiet. Outside voices can be loud.
steps: Use a whisper or a quiet voice inside.
Save your big yelling voice for outdoors.

items.say: A gentle voice sounds friendly and kind.
steps: Take a breath before you speak.
Use soft words.
Add a friendly smile.

items.t: Knowing when to pause a habit
items.say: A habit is something you do again and again. Sometimes it is time to pause.
steps: Set a timer on a phone or clock.
When the timer rings, go to another room.
Find something else to do.
items.o: Knowing when to pause a habit

items.t: Asking for help with strong urges
items.say: Sometimes your body wants to do something very, very much. A safe helper can help you pick something else.
steps: Tell a safe helper, "My body has a strong urge. Can you help me find something else to do?"
items.o: Asking for help with strong urges
